<reason>PRO (B) carried a double burden written into the motion: a measurable rise in transplants AND no increase in ethical violation or family distress. B argued the distress/ethics prong well — the dilemma in [B2.1], the "both systems guess" reframe, and the traceless-harm asymmetry in [B4.5]/[B5.1] are genuinely strong — but its affirmative prong never recovered. CON (A) broke the dilemma cleanly and early ("a rule can be unjust without being effective," [A2.1]), which meant B could no longer force a choice between inert default and ethical damage. A then pressed the causal isolation point hard: if the statute is merely "the political event that unlocks the machinery" [B2.3], then coordinators, not the consent rule, do the lifting, and the motion as written fails. B's answer — no reform ships naked, demanding a lab-pure default demands impossible evidence — is a fair reframe but concedes the attribution, and B's honest admission that Wales showed no jump [B4.3], while creditable for discipline, leaves the "measurably increase" element resting on cross-national clustering that A had already attributed to organization (Spain's law predating the rise). B's flagship kitchen-table example also took a direct hit that was never repaired: under the soft veto B itself defends, the same wife can still refuse, so presumed consent "only relabels the file" [A4.3]. A's weakest spot is that its ethical harm is admittedly unobservable in refusal or complaint data, and B exploited that skillfully; but since the motion requires PRO to prove the gain, an unproven benefit plus a contested intrinsic consent cost leaves A holding the cleaner decision rule. B also took a small execution cost from the clipped rebuttal.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's dismantling of B's dilemma and flagship hypothetical: "a rule can be unjust without being effective" plus "under the soft veto PRO still defends, the same wife can still refuse — presumed consent does not save that husband; it only relabels the file." That simultaneously freed A's ethics case from the effectiveness question and neutralized B's most vivid example.</best_rebuttal>
